record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₂, …, λₙ₊₁ be the first nontrivial Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues after λ₁. Must the scale-invariant sum |Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁) be at least the corresponding n-ball value C_n^{2/n} n j_{p+1,1}²? In dimension 2, this is the conjecture A(λ₂ + λ₃) ≥ [A(λ₂ + λ₃)]_disk = 2π j_{1,1}².

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² A(λ₂ + λ₃) ≥ [A(λ₂ + λ₃)]|disk = 2πj²_{1,1}, and for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ |Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁) ≥ [|Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)]|n-ball = C_n^{2/n} n j²_{p+1,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
$$0<\lambda_1(\Omega)<\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\lambda_3(\Omega)\le\cdots$$
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the numbers $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Let $|\Omega|$ denote the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$, and let $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a ball.

For $\nu\ge 0$, let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p=n/2-1$, so that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are given by squares of zeros of $J_{p+k}$ for $k\ge 0$, and in particular $\lambda_2(B)=\cdots=\lambda_{n+1}(B)$ all equal $j_{p+1,1}^2/R^2$ where $R$ is the radius of $B$. Writing $C_n=\omega_n j_{p,1}^n$ with $\omega_n$ the volume of the unit $n$-ball (so that $|B|^{2/n}\lambda_1(B)=C_n^{2/n}j_{p,1}^2$ in normalized form), the corresponding scale-invariant value for the ball $B^*$ of the same volume as $\Omega$ is
$$\bigl[\,|\Omega|^{2/n}\bigl(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}\bigr)\bigr]_{\text{$n$-ball}}=C_n^{2/n}\, n\, j_{p+1,1}^2.$$

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$|\Omega|^{2/n}\bigl(\lambda_2(\Omega)+\lambda_3(\Omega)+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)\bigr)\;\ge\;C_n^{2/n}\, n\, j_{p+1,1}^2,$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.

In particular, in dimension $n=2$, show that for every bounded planar domain $\Omega$ with area $A=|\Omega|$,
$$A\bigl(\lambda_2(\Omega)+\lambda_3(\Omega)\bigr)\;\ge\;2\pi\, j_{1,1}^2,$$
the right-hand side being the value attained when $\Omega$ is a disk.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a Faber–Krahn-type lower bound for the scale-invariant sum of the eigenvalues $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{n+1}$, conjectured to be minimized by the ball. The analogous Faber–Krahn result for $\lambda_1$ is classical, and the Ashbaugh–Benguria-type ratio inequalities are known, but the lower bound for the sum $\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}$ (and even the planar case $A(\lambda_2+\lambda_3)$) does not appear to be established in the literature. Recent surveys on shape optimization for Laplace eigenvalues continue to list this as an open problem; no proof or counterexample was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems on Dirichlet/Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues, including conjectured Faber–Krahn-type bounds for sums of low eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on Laplacian eigenvalues.

status_evidence.title: On the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Studies inequalities for sums of the eigenvalues $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{n+1}$ of the Dirichlet Laplacian compared with the ball.
status_evidence.claim: Related lower-order eigenvalue conjectures involving $\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}$ remain under active investigation.
